title: Alibaba's Open Source Code Leaks New Qwen4 AI Model Variants and 1 Million Token Window

tickers.name: Alibaba Group Holding Limited American Depositary Shares, each represents eight Ordinary Shares

summary:
Updates to Alibaba's open source Qwen repository have revealed two previously unannounced artificial intelligence models, a qwen4-coder-plus variant and a multimodal model named qwen4-omni-120b-think. The code, merged into the firm's coding agent repository on Oct. 28, also assigns a default context window of 1 million tokens to the Qwen4 family. These models were not listed in the company's official Qwen4 lineup, which consists of the Max, Plus, Flash and 27B versions.

The discovery follows a confirmation by Alibaba Cloud chief technology officer Feifei Li at the Apsara conference in Amsterdam that the Qwen4 series was scheduled for launch during the first week of November. While the new model names and technical defaults are visible in the codebase as of Nov. 3, no live endpoints for the models have been tested.

selectedTweets.bestBit: The change also gives every Qwen4 model a 1 million token context window, though the developer who wrote it calls that figure an inference.
selectedTweets.text:
‼️ Alibaba leaked the names of unreleased Qwen4 AI models in its own public code.

Code merged into Qwen Code, Alibaba's open-source coding agent, on 28 October names qwen4-coder-plus, and the repo's tests already use qwen4-omni-120b-think. Neither is among the four Qwen4 models Alibaba has announced.

The change also gives every Qwen4 model a 1 million token context window, though the developer who wrote it calls that figure an inference.

As of 3 November, the Qwen4 line is still in the code.

selectedTweets.bestBit: The repository's test fixtures also reference "qwen4-omni-120b-think", suggesting a multimodal reasoning variant is being prepared.
selectedTweets.text:
Qwen4 is showing up in @Alibaba_Qwen's own code, including an intriguing multimodal model name! 

A merged Qwen Code update gives Qwen4 models a default context window of 1 million tokens. The repository's test fixtures also reference "qwen4-omni-120b-think", suggesting a multimodal reasoning variant is being prepared.

These are concrete integration clues, but the context figure is still a client-side default, not a published model specification. No live Qwen4 endpoint was tested in the PR. A release could be approaching, though the code doesn't tell us when.
